summary: This informational document specifies SVG 1.2 RFC, an SVG profile for diagrams that can appear in RFCs, and considers issues around creating and using such diagrams. It was replaced by RFC 9896.

eli5.summary: Pictures in RFCs used to be drawn with typed characters. This sets the rules for using proper vector drawings instead. It has since been replaced by RFC 9896.

subtitle: A black-and-white, no-frills subset of SVG for line drawings in RFCs.

tldr.problem: RFCs were limited to ASCII art, but the new RFC format allows line drawings, and full SVG is far too rich for simple, permanent, accessible diagrams.
tldr.mechanism: SVG 1.2 RFC starts from SVG Tiny 1.2 and removes multimedia, interactivity, scripting, animation, metadata, extensibility and all color, leaving a small allowed list defined formally by a RELAX NG Compact schema.
tldr.outcome: It has been obsoleted by RFC 9896 and also updated by RFC 9920, so those are the documents to follow now.

today: RFC 7996 is an Informational document that has been obsoleted by RFC 9896, and RFC 9920 also updated it. Use RFC 9896 for the current SVG profile for RFCs.

sections.title: Why SVG in RFCs
sections.content:
The RFC Editor and the community have been changing the RFC format. RFC 6949 says graphics may include ASCII art and a more complex form to be defined, such as SVG line art. Color and grayscale will not be accepted, because RFCs must display correctly in monochrome for black-and-white displays and printing and for readers with visual disabilities.

RFC 7996 defines SVG 1.2 RFC, a profile (a subset) of SVG for RFC line drawings. Diagrams only support the text, which stays the normative description, and they should not be treated as complete specifications. The details are expected to change with experience, and other implementers must not expect those changes to be backwards-compatible.
sections.eli5: SVG is a way to describe pictures with shapes. Because RFCs must work for everyone, even on black-and-white printers, only a small, plain set of shapes is allowed.

sections.title: The SVG 1.2 RFC Profile
sections.content:
The starting point is SVG Tiny 1.2, a subset meant for small mobile devices. The profile then removes everything from these SVG Tiny 1.2 sections: Multimedia, Interactivity, Scripting, Animation, Metadata and Extensibility. Related attributes are removed too.

Basic shapes and text are allowed in full. Painting is allowed except anything relating to color. Links must be ASCII only (use the URI form of any IRI), and authors should link only to long-term stable URIs. Fonts are limited to the serif, sans-serif and monospace generic families, and the SVG font element is not allowed.

The allowed colors are a black-and-white subset: black, white, #000000 and #ffffff. The element list includes svg, g, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, path and text, among others.
sections.eli5: Start with a small toolbox made for phones, then take out the paint, the animations and the buttons. What is left is just lines, shapes and words in black and white.

sections.title: Creating and Checking Drawings
sections.content:
Packages such as Inkscape and Dia can produce SVG, but they may emit things SVG 1.2 RFC does not allow. For example, the marker attribute for arrowheads and the clipPath element are not allowed, so arrowheads must be drawn another way.

The RFC says a tool will be needed to strip disallowed content or replace values (for example Sans with sans-serif), and to list non-allowed keywords with context so authors can check conformance. A simple test version of such a tool was reported to work without visibly changing the diagrams. Including a drawing in an Internet-Draft depends on xml2rfc v3, as described in RFC 7991.

Appendix A gives the formal RELAX NG Compact schema. The RFC Editor website copy is considered definitive if there are discrepancies. The examples section shows a packet layout diagram (Figure 3 of RFC 793) and two sequence diagrams.
sections.eli5: Drawing programs often add fancy extras that are not allowed. A checker tool is needed to remove them and tell you what it changed.

sections.title: Accessibility and Security
sections.content:
A long-term goal is to make RFCs more accessible, for example to sight-impaired readers. Reading raw SVG code aloud seems unlikely to work, so authors are encouraged to provide alternative forms. SVG 1.2 RFC allows the title element (a brief caption), the desc element (a longer description) and the role attribute, and it points to guidance on using ARIA with SVG.

The Security Considerations section says the document does not introduce any security considerations on its own.
sections.eli5: Pictures need words too, so someone who cannot see the drawing can still have it described to them. That is what the title and description are for.
